abstract: Restriction-based algorithms for depth-two threshold circuits, as used in Williams' algorithmic method, depend on how many bottom linear threshold functions (LTFs) stay nonconstant on the $h$ live variables, and on how many distinct active-gate patterns arise over assignments to the fixed variables. Kane and Williams showed that a structured random restriction (one live variable in each of $h$ blocks) keeps an LTF active with probability $O(h/\sqrt N)$. We show that worst-case families meet this and stronger limits. If $h=o(\sqrt N)$ and $qh/\sqrt N\gg N$, there are $q$ sign-normal LTFs such that every restriction with $h$ live variables keeps $(\sqrt{2/\pi}+o(1))qh/\sqrt N$ gates active, uniformly. If $h=O(\sqrt{N-h})$ and $q/\sqrt{N-h}\gg N$, fixed-threshold sign-normal LTFs additionally make the active-gate set injective on all $2^{N-h}$ assignments, for every live set. For one live variable this injectivity is an exact-sphere separation problem on the cube $\{-1,1\}^M$. An entropy argument shows that sign-normal families need $\Omega(M^{3/2}/\log M)$ gates, and a hybrid construction (complete distance profiles for nearby pairs, a central window for distant pairs) uses $O(M^{3/2}/\sqrt{\log M})$ exact-radius spheres. The proofs are probabilistic and self-contained. A standard-library script checks the finite identities and the exact single-row separation probabilities for small parameters. These are worst-case obstructions to specific proof templates (one-gate activity bounds, pairwise regularity, column-by-column active-set compression). They give no circuit lower bound or algorithm, do not address higher-order joint structure, cover only the stated density regimes, and leave a $\sqrt{\log M}$ gap.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
1. The remark after the exact-sphere equivalence (density at h=1) now states the improvement only for one fixed live coordinate with thresholds varying across gates, which is what Theorem 4 proves; it says explicitly that the same improvement is not established for every live coordinate at a common threshold (the setting of Theorem 2).
2. The opening paragraph and the abstract now state that the Kane-Williams bound [2] is for a structured random restriction leaving one live variable in each of h blocks; the related-work paragraph already did.
3. Reference [9] updated to version 2 (https://rstation.ai/problems/computer_science/papers/1/v2), and its description now says that LTF outputs appear with unit coefficients in the character exponent with general internal weights, matching that version.
No theorem, proof or supplement file changed.
title: Uniform Active-Count Tightness and Exact-Sphere Separation for LTF Restrictions
